            mobile = container "Mobile Backend" "Serves the rental mobile app." "Kotlin"
            fleet = container "Fleet Service" "Tracks vehicle availability and locations." "Java"
            dispatch = container "Dispatch Service" "Assigns vehicles to bookings." "Java"
            pricing = container "Pricing Service" "Calculates rental prices." "Go"
            maintenance = container "Maintenance Service" "Plans servicing and repairs." "C#"
            telemetry = container "Telemetry Ingest" "Collects vehicle telemetry events." "Go"
            notifications = container "Notification Service" "Sends booking and reminder messages." "Python"
            contracts = container "Contract Service" "Manages rental contracts and deposits." "Java"
            damage = container "Damage Assessment" "Records and prices vehicle damage." "Python"
            reports = container "Reports Service" "Produces utilisation and revenue reports." "Java"
            search = container "Search Service" "Finds vehicles by location and class." "Go"
            scheduler = container "Batch Scheduler" "Runs the nightly pricing and maintenance batch." "Java"
            fleetdb = container "Fleet Database" "Stores vehicle and booking records." "PostgreSQL"
            customerdb = container "Customer Database" "Stores customer and contract records." "PostgreSQL"
            mediadb = container "Media Database" "Stores contracts, invoices, and damage photos." "PostgreSQL"
            queue = container "Event Queue" "Carries fleet events between the application parts." "Kafka"
            rates = container "Pricing Rules Library" "Computes rental prices from class, duration, and zone." "Python"
        }
        payments = element "Payment Provider" "Charges customer cards for rentals and deposits."
        telemetryFeed = element "Vehicle Telemetry Feed" "Streams position and status telemetry." "MQTT" "External"
        legacy = softwareSystem "Legacy Billing System" "The retired billing system being phased out."
        customer -> booking "Rents vehicles through" "HTTPS"
        customer -> mobile "Books vehicles via" "HTTPS"
        booking -> fleet "Reserves vehicles in" "gRPC"
        booking -> pricing "uses" "HTTP"
        mobile -> dispatch "Requests dispatch via" "gRPC"
        fleet -> scheduler "Registers nightly tasks in" "gRPC"
        pricing -> rates "Looks up rules in" "in-process"
        contracts -> payments "Charges cards through" "REST/JSON"
        damage -> mediadb "Stores damage photos in" "SQL"
        reports -> fleetdb "Reads booking records from" "SQL"
        maintenance -> fleetdb "Stores service records in" "SQL"
        search -> fleetdb "Reads availability from" "SQL"
        contracts -> customerdb "Stores contract records in" "SQL"
        telemetry -> queue "Publishes telemetry events to" "Kafka"
        queue -> notifications "Delivers booking events to" "Kafka"
        telemetry -> telemetryFeed "Receives fleet telemetry from" "MQTT"
    }
    views {
        systemContext manager "CustomerContext" "Shows the customer's journey around the system." {
            include *
            autoLayout
        }
        container manager {
            include *
            autoLayout
        }
    }
}`;

const [validate, inspect] = await Promise.allSettled([
  tools.structurizr.validate({ dsl }),
  tools.structurizr.inspect({ dsl }),
]);

return {

  inspect: inspect.status === "fulfilled" ? inspect.value : inspect.reason,
};

part.text:
I read the model and ran it through the Structurizr validator/inspector (read-only — no files touched). It parses and validates as DSL, but as a C4 document it has real completeness and consistency problems. Findings below.

## Element types & modeling

- **`payments` (Payment Provider)** is declared as a generic `element` rather than a `softwareSystem`, and is not tagged `External`. In C4 an external system like a payment provider is a software system; a bare element loses that semantics and won't be treated/rendered as an external system in views.
- **`telemetryFeed` (Vehicle Telemetry Feed)** is also a generic `element` (it does carry the `External` tag, but the type is still wrong). It should be a `softwareSystem` so it's modeled and rendered as an external system.
- **`rates` (Pricing Rules Library)** is modeled as a `container`, but a library is neither a deployable unit nor a data store — it's a component-level concept. The `pricing -> rates "in-process"` relationship confirms it isn't separately deployed, so it should be a component inside `pricing` (or omitted at container level), not a container.
- **`legacy` (Legacy Billing System)** is disconnected — no relationships to/from any element, and it appears on no view (both flagged as errors by the inspector). A "retired system being phased out" with no connections adds noise without conveying anything; either model the relationships that justify its presence (e.g. data migration, or `contracts -> legacy`) or remove it.

## Naming & descriptions

- **`mediadb` (Media Database)** has a name/description mismatch: it's called a "Media Database" but described as storing "contracts, invoices, and damage photos." Contracts and invoices are business records, not media. Only `damage -> mediadb` (photos) is actually drawn, so the contracts/invoices part is both misnamed and unsupported.
- **`booking -> pricing`** has the relationship description `"uses"`, which is too vague to be informative. C4 relationship descriptions should be meaningful verb phrases (e.g. "Calculates prices for bookings using"); "uses" tells the reader nothing about the interaction.

## Missing relationships (completeness & consistency)

- **`dispatch` (Dispatch Service)** has no outgoing relationships. It "assigns vehicles to bookings" and receives requests from `mobile`, but never interacts with `fleet` (to assign/check vehicles) or `booking` (to record the assignment) — a dead end, so the model doesn't show how dispatch actually works.
- **`notifications` (Notification Service)** has no outgoing relationships. It "sends booking and reminder messages" and receives events from `queue`, but there's no relationship showing where the messages go (to the `customer`, or to an external email/SMS provider) — a dead end.
- **`search` (Search Service)** has no incoming relationships. It "finds vehicles by location and class" and reads `fleetdb`, but nothing calls it — an orphan, so the model doesn't show who uses search.
- **`contracts` (Contract Service)** has no incoming relationships. It "manages rental contracts and deposits" and writes to `customerdb`/`payments`, but nothing creates a contract (presumably `booking` when a customer books) — an orphan.
- **`scheduler` (Batch Scheduler)** is described as running "the nightly pricing and maintenance batch," but there are no `scheduler -> pricing` or `scheduler -> maintenance` relationships. Its stated purpose isn't reflected in the model (only `fleet -> scheduler` is drawn, which is the reverse of the expected direction).
- **`queue` (Event Queue)** is described as carrying "fleet events," but the only delivery relationship is `queue -> notifications "Delivers booking events to"`, and no container publishes booking events to the queue (only `telemetry` publishes telemetry events). The event flow is inconsistent and incomplete — the source of the "booking events" is missing.
- **`fleetdb` (Fleet Database)** is described as storing "vehicle and booking records," but no container writes vehicle or booking records to it — only `maintenance` writes service records. The description overstates what's actually modeled.
- **`customerdb` (Customer Database)** is described as storing "customer and contract records," but only `contracts` writes to it (contract records). There's no source for the customer-records part of the description.
- **`damage` (Damage Assessment)** "records and prices vehicle damage," but the only relationship drawn is `damage -> mediadb` (photos). There's no relationship showing where damage records are stored or how damage is priced (e.g. to `pricing`/`rates`), so the stated purpose is only partially reflected.
- **`reports` (Reports Service)** "produces utilisation and revenue reports," but it only reads `fleetdb`. There's no relationship showing who consumes the reports (a dead end), and revenue data lives in `customerdb` (contracts), which it doesn't read.

## Views & workspace

- **The container view** (`container manager`) has no explicit name — it gets an auto-generated key (`Container-001`) that the inspector warns isn't stable over time — and no description. It should be given a name and description, like the system context view has.
- **The workspace** has no defined scope (flagged as an error by the inspector). Since the model is a single software system with containers, the scope should be set to `SoftwareSystem`.

The one view that's well-specified is the system context view (`CustomerContext`), which has both a name and a description. The file on disk is unchanged.
